text: I fired my therapist because she told me I need to have more empathy for straight white men. It was our third session. We were still getting to know each other. And she said, I noticed that you joke about straight white men a lot. Have you thought about having more empathy for them? And I was like, have you thought about quitting your job? Straight white men are the one group of people that have consistently and intentionally caused myself women that I love and the whole world the most amount of harm. And I should be allowed to vent those frustrations in a safe, nonjudgmental place like therapy. You know, it amazes me how oblivious some people still are to the concepts of racism and sexism in 2026. For anyone who doesn't understand what I mean, when you judge, mock, or express hostility towards an entire group of people based on their skin color or sex, that is racial and sex-based prejudice. And under the ordinary definitions of those words, it is racism and sexism. And if you do not see the problem, try changing white to another race or skin color, Asian, black, brown, whatever, and change men to women. Suddenly, the statement sounds outrageous, doesn't it? And some will probably say, well, it's not the same. Of course, the historical and social context may not be identical, but the fundamental principle is the same. You are assigning collective guilt to millions of individuals because of the race and sex they were born with. You can criticize historical systems. You can criticize governments, institutions, ideologies, or particular people. You can discuss the fact that certain groups have historically held more power. But none of that makes every individual of a particular race or gender responsible for everything other individuals in that group have ever done. And then there's the entitlement of going to a professional because you supposedly want help dealing with your issues. The therapist notices a pattern, asks whether you have considered having more empathy for the people you constantly joke about, and your response is essentially, have you considered quitting your job? You are obviously allowed to fire your therapist. But therapy is not supposed to be a place where another person simply validates everything you already believe. Sometimes, a therapist is going to question your behavior, challenge your assumptions, or point out something that makes you uncomfortable. And then, instead of reflecting on the question, you fire her and make a public video about how ridiculous it was for her to even suggest that you should have empathy for an entire category of human beings? Honestly, I am normally quite skeptical of therapists, but this one seems to deserve some praise. Overall, here's what I want to say. Guys, please try to judge people based on their character, their actions, their behavior, and how they treat other people. Not based on their skin color, sex, sexuality, social status, or any other category they happen to belong to. Try to treat people as individuals. Try to be decent human beings. And guys, in the end, I wanted to quickly express a special gratitude to the paid subscribers of my channel. As of today, there are 22 people who directly support my channel and receive exclusive videos, priority direct messages, and access to the special member's channel. If you want to support me and my work, please become a paid subscriber too.
